deep_analysis.executive_intro:
The FTSE screen is broadly cautious: 147 names sit on Hold versus 61 actionable Buys (16 Strong Buy, 45 Buy) and 40 Avoids, so value signals are selective rather than market-wide. All five top candidates are Strong Buys with full data quality (20/20 metrics) and pass all five model families (cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk), but conviction scores are modest (51–55%) and every pick is a new signal (one week at rating). Sector clustering is pronounced—three of five leaders are Industrials (FirstGroup, ME Group, Grafton)—with Healthcare (Hikma) and Communication Services (ITV) providing partial diversification. A key data limitation: several model reason strings show implausible yield figures (e.g. 396%, 790%), while headline metrics show 4.0–7.9%; treat dividend and some growth inputs as requiring manual verification, and note Graham Net-Net failed for all top names due to missing NCAV balance-sheet data.

**FGP.L (FirstGroup plc)** — Eleven of 22 models passed (composite 90%, sector-relative 85%), led by Earnings Yield (E/P 11.0%, P/E 9.1), FCF Yield (31.3%), Composite Value, Piotroski F-Score (8/9), and Earnings Quality (FCF/NI 2.56). Key metrics: P/E 9.1, P/B 1.4, yield 4.0%, ROE 16.7%. Failures include Financial Health (high debt-to-equity, weak liquidity), Graham Enterprising (excessive leverage, negative earnings growth −5.9%), and Economic Moat. Adds to Industrials concentration among top picks. **Verdict: watchlist** — exceptional headline cheapness and cash conversion, but leverage, liquidity, and declining earnings warrant confirmation before sizing.

**MEGP.L (ME Group International plc)** — Fourteen of 22 models passed (composite 81%, sector-relative 89%), the broadest pass rate in the top five. Standouts include Graham Enterprising, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Economic Moat (ROE 28.2%, margin 17.6%, D/E 28%), High Dividend Yield (7.9%), and Magic Formula. Key metrics: P/E 7.1, P/B 2.0, yield 7.9%, ROE 28.2%. Fails FCF Yield (3.9% vs 5% threshold), Earnings Quality (weak free-cash conversion), and Lynch PEG (negative earnings growth −3.9%); price is below the 200-day MA in a downtrend. Second Industrials name in the cluster. **Verdict: watchlist** — rare combination of deep value and quality scores, but negative earnings growth and sub-par FCF conversion need a fundamental explanation.

**HIK.L (Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC)** — Thirteen of 22 models passed (composite 75%, sector-relative 91%), including Graham Enterprising, Lynch PEG (PEG 0.49, growth 23.5%), Quality Value, Magic Formula, and Financial Health (D/E 62%, coverage 7.2x). Key metrics: P/E 11.6, P/B 1.8, yield 3.9%, ROE 16.5%. Critical failures: FCF Yield (−2.0%; reported FCF −£66.1m), Earnings Quality (weak free-cash conversion), and Piotroski F-Score (6/9). Only Healthcare name among top picks, which reduces Industrials concentration slightly. **Verdict: pass** — attractive earnings-growth and valuation multiples are undercut by negative free cash flow and weak cash conversion.

**GFTU.L (Grafton Group plc)** — Eleven of 22 models passed (composite 84%, sector-relative 80%), notably Graham Defensive, Graham Enterprising, Schloss Low P/B (P/B 1.09), FCF Yield (10.0%), Piotroski F-Score (8/9), Earnings Quality, and Financial Health (D/E 38%, current ratio 2.11). Key metrics: P/E 12.6, P/B 1.1, yield 4.0%, ROE 8.4%. Misses on ROE-driven quality screens (Buffett Quality, Economic Moat) and Magic Formula; RSI 63 flagged as elevated. Third Industrials pick—sector concentration risk is material if building multiple names from this list. **Verdict: accumulate** — the cleanest balance-sheet and Graham-profile fit in the group, with moderate valuation and positive earnings growth (8.4%), despite modest ROE.

**ITV.L (ITV plc)** — Fourteen of 22 models passed (composite 83%, sector-relative 80%), including Earnings Yield, FCF Yield (9.1%), Lynch PEG (PEG 0.48, growth 25.6%), High Dividend Yield (6.8%), Quality Value, Composite Value, and Financial Health (D/E 48%, interest coverage 15.1x). Key metrics: P/E 12.2, P/B 1.5, yield 6.8%, ROE 12.3%. Sole top pick with “accumulate” timing (RSI 36, below 200-day MA). Piotroski F-Score is a stark 3/9 (leverage not declining, margins and turnover deteriorating). Communication Services exposure diversifies away from Industrials. **Verdict: watchlist** — favourable entry timing and strong dividend/FCF profile, but deteriorating financial trend scores argue for qualitative work before committing capital.

- FGP.L: Public-transport operator—franchise renewal and regulatory pricing risk are not in the screen; UK bus/rail operators often carry defined-benefit pension obligations (open question: deficit size and funding trajectory); earnings growth is negative (−5.9%) despite value flags, suggesting possible cyclical or contract-timing headwinds; governance and capital-allocation history post-restructuring are not assessed here.
- MEGP.L: Revenue tied to travel, leisure, and unattended retail (photo booths)—high cyclicality and post-pandemic normalisation risk; negative earnings growth (−3.9%) with a 7.9% yield raises dividend sustainability questions not captured by quantitative filters; business-model durability versus digital substitution is an open question.
- HIK.L: Generic injectables/pharma—patent cliffs, FDA and international regulatory actions, and pricing pressure are absent from the screen; negative FCF (−£66.1m) may reflect capex, M&A, or working-capital swings that the screen cannot classify; leverage (D/E 62%) passed quantitative thresholds but may be elevated for a pharma balance sheet under stress.
- GFTU.L: Building-materials merchant—directly exposed to UK/Ireland construction and housing cycles; low ROE (8.4%) may signal thin competitive moat despite passing Graham screens; acquisition-led growth history (implied by merchant roll-up model) carries integration and goodwill impairment risk not modelled here.
- GFTU.L / sector cluster: Three Industrials in the top five—macro slowdown or rates-driven construction weakness would hit multiple picks simultaneously.
- ITV.L: Advertising revenue is highly cyclical and structurally challenged by streaming shift; Ofcom/public-service broadcasting obligations and potential regulatory change are not screened; Piotroski 3/9 suggests deteriorating operational trends despite strong headline metrics; pension scheme status and content-investment commitments are open balance-sheet questions.
deep_analysis.red_flags:
NAMES WORTH DEEPER RESEARCH

- ITV.L — With Piotroski 3/9 but 14/22 model passes and “accumulate” timing, is the 6.8% dividend and 25.6% earnings growth sustainable through an advertising downcycle, or is the screen catching a peak?
- FGP.L — Does the 31.3% FCF yield reflect durable owner earnings, or one-off working-capital/capex effects in a leveraged transport business with negative earnings growth?
- MEGP.L — What explains negative earnings growth (−3.9%) and weak FCF conversion alongside Economic Moat and Buffett Quality passes—is the 7.9% yield a value trap or a genuine payout supported by cash flows?

documents.name: ME Group International plc
documents.executive_summary: ME Group operates a global estate of ~49,700 instant-service vending machines (photobooths, laundry, printing and ancillary services) across 16 countries, with a long track record of cash generation and shareholder distributions. The quantitative screen flags a strong buy on cheapness (P/E 7.1, yield 7.9%), quality (ROE 28.2%, low leverage), and dividend/GARP metrics, against a share price trading below its 200-day moving average with neutral timing. The investment case rests on a structurally growing, high-margin laundry franchise (Wash.ME) diversifying earnings away from a mature but still cash-rich photobooth estate (Photo.ME), at a valuation that embeds little growth. The central debate is whether April’s French consumer slowdown and photobooth regulatory headwinds (notably Germany) are transitory — management guides FY2026 PBT of £69–74m versus record FY2025 PBT of £78.2m — or the start of a more persistent earnings reset that would challenge dividend sustainability at current payout levels.
documents.investment_thesis:
The screen’s strong-buy signal (14/22 models passing; composite 81%, sector-relative 89%; families: cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk) aligns with a business that exhibits classic value characteristics: recurring, site-based revenue; high EBITDA margins (~38% at group level); net cash balance sheet; and a stated policy to return more than 55% of annual profit after tax (FY2025 total dividend 8.64p, 58% of EPS).

Business quality supports the screen’s quality and financial-health passes. FY2025 (filings) delivered record PBT of £78.2m on revenue of £315.4m, with cash generated from operations of £115.5m and net cash of £26.5m (excluding lease liabilities). Wash.ME is the growth engine: FY2025 laundry EBITDA rose 18.1% to £55.5m (46% of group EBITDA), with 1,145 net machine additions. ROE of 28.2% and debt/equity of ~28% (screen) reflect disciplined capital allocation into machines with targeted payback periods exceeding cost of capital, per management commentary.

The valuation hook is straightforward: at ~7x earnings and ~8% yield, the market prices ME Group as a declining photobooth operator rather than a hybrid laundry/photobooth compounder. If FY2026 PBT stabilises within the revised £69–74m range and the laundry rollout (c.1,300 installations planned; landmark ASDA partnership targeting up to 700 UK sites) continues, current multiples offer meaningful re-rating optionality without requiring heroic growth assumptions. The screen’s neutral timing (RSI 44, below 200-day MA) suggests no urgency to chase, consistent with a staged accumulation approach.
documents.financial_review:
*Primary source: filing bodies. Yahoo for FCF cross-checks only.*

FY2023–FY2025 shows consistent revenue and profit growth through FY2025 (revenue £315.4m, PBT £78.2m, EBITDA margin 38.2%). Wash.ME vending revenue reached £100.8m (+10.2%); laundry EBITDA £55.5m (46% of group). Photo.ME vending revenue fell 4.0% to £166.2m. Since 2021, Wash.ME’s share of vending revenue rose from 24.4% to 35.0% and EBITDA share from 34.7% to 46.1% (Annual Report 2025).

**Cash and dividends:** FY2025 cash from operations £115.5m; net operating cash £90.8m; capex £65.6m; FCF £25.2m (Yahoo); dividends paid £29.8m. Operating cash covered dividends ~3.0×; reported FCF ~0.85× — explaining the screen’s FCF Yield and Earnings Quality fails. Policy targets >55% of PAT (FY2025 payout 58%). Interim dividend cut to 3.60p (−6.5%) signals adjustment as FY2026 PBT is guided to £69–74m.

**H1 FY2026:** Revenue flat (+0.3%); EBITDA +7.1% on laundry mix; PBT −3.8%; EPS −3.9%; cash from operations −18.9% on inventory build (+£8.3m); net cash £7.5m (from £26.5m). May/June recovery followed April French weakness.

documents.name: Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC
documents.executive_summary: Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC is a FTSE 100 generic and specialty pharmaceutical group with a diversified three-segment model (Injectables, Branded MENA, Hikma Rx US retail), reporting FY2025 group revenue of $3,349m and core operating profit of $741m. The quantitative screen rates the stock a strong buy on cheapness (P/E ~11.6, yield ~3.9%), quality (ROE ~16.5%, ROIC 16.0%), dividend growth, GARP, and financial health, with 13 of 22 models passing. The valuation hook is a cyclically depressed multiple on a business that still generates solid cash, carries investment-grade leverage (net debt/core EBITDA 1.6x), and has announced a $250m share buyback alongside a 5% dividend increase. The central debate is whether Injectables margin erosion, withdrawn medium-term guidance, and a softer 2026 outlook are a temporary reset or a structural de-rating of a formerly premium compounder.
documents.investment_thesis:
For a value investor, Hikma offers a rare combination of screen passes across five factor families — cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk — with full data completeness (20/20 metrics). At roughly 11–12x earnings and ~1.8x book, the market prices in sustained margin pressure rather than business failure; that is consistent with a contrarian entry if normalisation is achievable.

Business quality remains defensible. Hikma is a top-tier US generic injectables supplier by volume, the largest pharma company by sales in MENA (per IQVIA data cited in filings), and generates 16.0% ROIC with BBB/stable ratings from S&P and Fitch. Branded grew core revenue 10% with core operating margin 26.4%; Hikma Rx held revenue flat at $1,037m while expanding core margin to 17.3%. The group launched 84 products in 2025, entered US biosimilars (ustekinumab), and is investing in differentiated injectables (Tyzavan®). US manufacturing footprint is a strategic asset amid proposed generic drug tariffs — a point echoed in recent sell-side commentary.

The screen’s strong buy signal aligns with a classic “quality at a reasonable price” setup: low P/E plus high yield (Neff PEGY, Low P/E + High Yield), Buffett-style quality metrics, and financial health (D/E ~62%). Timing is neutral (RSI ~57, price above 200-day SMA), so the case is fundamental rather than momentum-driven. Capital return supports the thesis: total dividend raised to 84 cents (+5%) and a $250m buyback planned for 2026.

The offset is that core profit growth is slowing (core EPS +2% in 2025) and management withdrew medium-term group and Injectables margin guidance after a strategic review — a governance and credibility overhang that screens alone cannot capture.

documents.executive_summary: Grafton Group is a pan-European merchanting group (building materials, DIY, plumbing/heating) that the quantitative screen rates **Strong Buy** (11/22 models, composite 84%), driven by cheapness (P/E 12.6, P/B 1.1), dividend yield (~4.0%), FCF generation, and balance-sheet liquidity (current ratio 2.11). Yahoo-sourced financials show FY2025 revenue recovery (+10.4% to £2,519.6m) and net income up to £136.6m, with continued buybacks and a new £25m repurchase programme, but earnings remain well below the 2022 peak (£208.6m). The valuation hook is a cash-generative distributor trading modestly above book with shareholder returns (dividend + buybacks) and Iberia/Ireland offsetting UK weakness. The key debate is whether margin normalisation and European M&A integration justify re-rating, or whether cyclical UK construction and lease-adjusted leverage cap returns — a question this pack cannot fully resolve without primary RNS/annual report extracts.
documents.investment_thesis:
For a value investor, Grafton fits several classic screens simultaneously: Graham Defensive/Enterprising, Schloss Low P/B, FCF Yield, Neff PEGY, Dividend Growth, Dreman Contrarian, Piotroski F-Score, Composite Value, Earnings Quality, and Financial Health — spanning cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk families (5/4 passed). At P/E 12.6 and P/B 1.09, the market prices in modest growth and cyclical risk rather than franchise quality.

Business quality indicators from Yahoo (fallback): consistent operating cash flow (£217–272m annually, 2022–2025), FCF of £205.6m in FY2025, net cash/investment buffer (£396m cash plus £100m short-term investments vs £221m gross borrowings ex-leases), and a shrinking share count (223.4m ordinary shares in 2022 to 191.3m in 2025) via sustained buybacks (£57m in 2025; £159m in 2023). Revenue re-accelerated in 2025 after a flat/down 2023–2024 period, consistent with management commentary (via news) of Iberia and Ireland driving growth while the UK remains challenging.

The screen’s FCF yield and financial-health passes align with a capital-allocation story: management returned capital through dividends (~£73m/year) and buybacks while maintaining liquidity and funding bolt-on M&A (£17–69m/year, 2022–2025).
